title: Stochastic Approximation Approach for Decentralized Optimization on Time Varying Random Networks
claim: Our methods reach lower error and loss than all baselines for the same communication budget, even with heavily sparsified communication.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared legend on top, log-log axes
description: A wide legend box across the top lists ten methods. Our two methods, FSPDA-SA and FSPDA-STORM, are drawn as thick solid blue and orange lines. The baselines are thinner dashed lines in other colors: K-GT, LED, Decen-Scaffnew, DSGD, Swarm-SGD and CHOCO-SGD. Below the legend are three log-log line plots that share the x-axis, Bits Transmitted, which runs from about 10^10 to 10^12. The y-axes are Gradient Norm Squared, Train Loss and Consensus Error. Every curve falls as more bits are sent. The thick orange and blue lines end in star markers at the lowest values. CHOCO-SGD (gray) stays high, and Swarm-SGD (pink) and DSGD (cyan) plateau or oscillate. The eye goes first to the thick colored curves and the stars at the bottom right of each panel.
caption: Feed-forward neural network classification training on MNIST using $10^6$ iterations.
abstract: This paper initiates the study of a stochastic approximation approach with the Fully Stochastic Primal Dual Algorithm (FSPDA) framework for decentralized optimization on random and time varying topologies. Our framework relies on a novel observation that randomnesses in time varying topology can be incorporated into a stochastic equality constrained optimization formulation. We derived two new algorithms supporting sparsified communication on time varying topologies --- FSPDA-SA allows agents to execute multiple local gradient steps to accelerate convergence, and FSPDA-STORM further incorporates variance reduction to improve sample complexity. For problems with smooth (possibly non-convex) objective function, within $T$ iterations, FSPDA-SA (resp. FSPDA-STORM) finds an $\mathcal{O}( 1/\sqrt{T} )$-stationary (resp. $\mathcal{O}( 1/T^{2/3} )$) solution. Our methods are the first to establish finite-time stationarity guarantees in smooth nonconvex decentralized stochastic optimization over i.i.d. random subgraphs (such as disconnected subgraphs at every iteration) of a fixed connected base graph without bounded local function heterogeneity.
